passages.text: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
passages.sermon: Wine mocks people.\r\nStrong drink causes fights.\r\nAnyone who lets wine or strong drink lead them astray is not wise.
passages.original: לֵ֣ץ הַ֭יַּין הֹמֶ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְכָל־ שֹׁ֥גֶה בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א יֶחְכָּֽם׃

passages.text: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.
passages.sermon:
A king is powerful and dangerous.
His anger is terrifying.
His terror is like the roar of a lion.
If someone provokes the king, that person sins against his own life.
Whoever angers the king risks losing his life.
passages.original: נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר אֵ֣ימַת מֶ֑לֶךְ מִ֝תְעַבְּר֗וֹ חוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.
passages.sermon:
A wise man seeks honor.
He avoids arguments.
A fool starts fights.
A fool exposes himself by quarreling.
passages.original: כָּב֣וֹד לָ֭אִישׁ שֶׁ֣בֶת מֵרִ֑יב וְכָל־ אֱ֝וִ֗יל יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃

passages.text: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
A slacker does not plow the field when it is time to work.
He waits until harvest time.
He looks for crops at harvest.
He finds nothing.
passages.original: מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא־ יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ יִשְׁאַל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן׃

passages.text: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.
passages.sermon:
A man’s heart holds intentions.
These intentions are like deep waters.
A man of understanding can draw out these intentions.
passages.original: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב־ אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
passages.sermon:
Many people say they are loyal.
Many people claim to show kindness.
Few people are truly trustworthy.
It is hard to find a faithful person.
passages.original: רָב־ אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא׃

passages.text: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man lives with integrity.
He acts honestly.
He does what is right.
His children receive blessing after him.
His children benefit because of his integrity.
passages.original: מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.
passages.sermon:
A king sits on a throne to judge.
He looks carefully at everything.
He sees all evil.
He removes all evil.
passages.original: מֶ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־ כִּסֵּא־ דִ֑ין מְזָרֶ֖ה בְעֵינָ֣יו כָּל־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?
passages.sermon:
No person can say, "I have kept my heart pure."
No person can say, "I am cleansed from my sin."
Every person has sinned.
No one is completely pure in heart.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יֹ֭אמַר זִכִּ֣יתִי לִבִּ֑י טָ֝הַ֗רְתִּי מֵחַטָּאתִֽי׃

passages.text: Differing weights and unequal measures — both are detestable to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God hates dishonesty.
\r\nGod detests differing weights.
\r\nGod detests unequal measures.
\r\nGod rejects both kinds of dishonesty.
passages.original: אֶ֣בֶן וָ֭אֶבֶן אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.
passages.sermon:
A young man shows who he is by what he does.
People see his actions.
People know if his actions are pure.
People know if his actions are upright.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם בְּ֭מַעֲלָלָיו יִתְנַכֶּר־ נָ֑עַר אִם־ זַ֖ךְ וְאִם־ יָשָׁ֣ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD made everything.
The LORD made ears that hear.
The LORD made eyes that see.
The LORD made both ears and eyes.
passages.original: אֹ֣זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת וְעַ֣יִן רֹאָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה גַם־ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.
passages.sermon:
Do not love sleep.
If you love sleep, you will become poor.
Open your eyes.
If you open your eyes, you will have plenty of food.
passages.original: אַל־ תֶּֽאֱהַ֣ב שֵׁ֭נָה פֶּן־ תִּוָּרֵ֑שׁ פְּקַ֖ח עֵינֶ֣יךָ שְֽׂבַֽע־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer, but on the way out, he gloats.
passages.sermon:
A buyer speaks.
The buyer says, “Worthless! Worthless!”
He says this about what he wants to buy.
He tries to lower the value.
He wants a better price.
After he buys it, he leaves.
Then he boasts about his purchase.
He feels proud of his gain.
passages.original: רַ֣ע רַ֭ע יֹאמַ֣ר הַקּוֹנֶ֑ה וְאֹזֵ֥ל ל֝֗וֹ אָ֣ז יִתְהַלָּֽל׃

passages.text: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.
passages.sermon:
Gold exists in abundance.
Many rubies also exist.
Lips that speak knowledge are rare.
Lips of knowledge are a valuable treasure.
passages.original: יֵ֣שׁ זָ֭הָב וְרָב־ פְּנִינִ֑ים וּכְלִ֥י יְ֝קָ֗ר שִׂפְתֵי־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
passages.sermon:
A person may promise to pay a debt for a stranger.
This person puts up security for someone he does not know.
Take his garment as a pledge.
If he guarantees a foreigner, require collateral from him.
passages.original: לְֽקַח־ בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־ עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִים חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.
passages.sermon:
A man eats food he gained by fraud.
He thinks this food tastes sweet.
Later, his mouth fills with gravel.
The pleasure turns into pain.
passages.original: עָרֵ֣ב לָ֭אִישׁ לֶ֣חֶם שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝אַחַ֗ר יִמָּֽלֵא־ פִ֥יהוּ חָצָֽץ׃

passages.text: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.
passages.sermon:
Wise people make plans with advice from others.
Good plans need careful consultation.
If you must go to war, seek guidance from wise counselors.
Sound guidance leads to success in battle.
passages.original: מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּעֵצָ֣ה תִכּ֑וֹן וּ֝בְתַחְבֻּל֗וֹת עֲשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
passages.sermon:
A gossip reveals secrets.
A gossip cannot keep things private.
A gossip talks about others.
A person who babbles with his lips speaks carelessly.
Do not associate with a person who babbles.
Avoid people who cannot keep secrets.
passages.original: גּֽוֹלֶה־ סּ֭וֹד הוֹלֵ֣ךְ רָכִ֑יל וּלְפֹתֶ֥ה שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִתְעָרָֽב׃

passages.text: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
passages.sermon:
A person who curses his father or his mother acts with disrespect.
This person rejects the honor due to parents.
God sees this as a serious offense.
The lamp of this person will go out.
He will lose his light.
He will be left in the deepest darkness.
He will have no guidance or blessing.
passages.original: מְ֭קַלֵּל אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֑וֹ יִֽדְעַ֥ךְ נֵ֝ר֗וֹ בְּאִישׁוֹן חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.
passages.sermon:
An inheritance is property or wealth received from someone who has died.
Some people gain an inheritance quickly.
They receive it without waiting or working for it.
This kind of inheritance will not be blessed in the end.
It will not bring lasting good.
passages.original: נַ֭חֲלָה מְבֻחֶלֶת בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ לֹ֣א תְבֹרָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
passages.sermon:
Do not say, “I will repay this evil.”
Do not seek revenge for wrongs done to you.
Trust in the LORD.
Wait for the LORD to act.
The LORD will save you.
passages.original: אַל־ תֹּאמַ֥ר אֲשַׁלְּמָה־ רָ֑ע קַוֵּ֥ה לַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה וְיֹ֣שַֽׁע לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.
passages.sermon:
The LORD hates unequal weights.
The LORD finds dishonest measures detestable.
Dishonest scales are not good.
God rejects all forms of cheating in trade.
passages.original: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן וּמֹאזְנֵ֖י מִרְמָ֣ה לֹא־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?
passages.sermon: The LORD directs a man’s steps.\r\nA man cannot fully understand his own path.
passages.original: מֵיהוָ֥ה מִצְעֲדֵי־ גָ֑בֶר וְ֝אָדָ֗ם מַה־ יָּבִ֥ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.
passages.sermon:
A man can make a vow to God quickly.
He may promise something holy without thinking.
This is dangerous.
Later, the man may want to change his promise.
He may try to reconsider his vow after making it.
This is a trap for him.
passages.original: מוֹקֵ֣שׁ אָ֭דָם יָ֣לַע קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאַחַ֖ר נְדָרִ֣ים לְבַקֵּֽר׃

passages.text: A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
passages.sermon:
A wise king rules the people.
He identifies the wicked people.
He separates the wicked from others.
He punishes the wicked.
He crushes them like grain under a threshing wheel.
passages.original: מְזָרֶ֣ה רְ֭שָׁעִים מֶ֣לֶךְ חָכָ֑ם וַיָּ֖שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם אוֹפָֽן׃

passages.text: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.
passages.sermon:
God uses the human spirit as His lamp.
God searches every part of a person through this spirit.
God sees into the deepest places inside a person.
God knows all that is within a person.
passages.original: נֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה נִשְׁמַ֣ת אָדָ֑ם חֹ֝פֵ֗שׂ כָּל־ חַדְרֵי־ בָֽטֶן׃

passages.text: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.
passages.sermon:
A king needs loving devotion and faithfulness.
Loving devotion and faithfulness keep the king safe.
Loving devotion and faithfulness help the king stay on his throne.
A king rules well when he shows loving devotion and faithfulness.
passages.original: חֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ־ מֶ֑לֶךְ וְסָעַ֖ד בַּחֶ֣סֶד כִּסְאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.
passages.sermon:
Young men have strength.
This strength is their glory.
Old men have gray hair.
Gray hair is the splendor of old men.
passages.original: תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בַּחוּרִ֣ים כֹּחָ֑ם וַהֲדַ֖ר זְקֵנִ֣ים שֵׂיבָֽה׃

passages.text: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.
passages.sermon:
Lashes remove evil.
Wounds drive out wrongdoing.
Beatings cleanse a person deeply.
They reach the inmost parts.
passages.original: חַבֻּר֣וֹת פֶּ֭צַע תַּמְרִיק בְּרָ֑ע וּ֝מַכּ֗וֹת חַדְרֵי־ בָֽטֶן׃
